info.title: Akeru Bot public metadata API
info.summary: Read-only public metadata for Akeru Bot project files.
info.description:
Read-only public metadata for Akeru Bot project files. Akeru Bot itself runs on the user's machine and does not expose a hosted automation API.

Versioning: every operation lives under a major version prefix in the URL path, starting at `/v1`. A breaking change to a response shape ships under a new prefix such as `/v2`; additive fields ship in place. The unversioned `/schema/t3.json` path stays as an alias for `$schema` references in editors and is not part of the version contract.

Deprecation: a deprecated operation returns `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers (RFC 9745 and RFC 8594), is marked `deprecated: true` in this document, and keeps serving for at least 6 months after the `Deprecation` date. The successor is linked from the response `Link` header with `rel="successor-version"`.

Rate limits: responses carry `RateLimit-Policy` and `RateLimit` headers (the IETF RateLimit header fields). The published policy is 600 requests per 60 second window per client. A throttled request returns `429` with `Retry-After` in seconds.

get.summary: Get the Akeru Bot project-file schema
get.description: Returns the JSON Schema used to validate t3.json project configuration files. The endpoint is unauthenticated, read-only, and does not touch user data.

get.summary: Get the project-file schema from the unversioned alias
get.description: Same document as GET /v1/schema/t3.json. This path exists so t3.json files can reference the schema from a stable URL in editors. Call the versioned path from code.

RateLimitPolicy.description: Published quota for this endpoint, as the IETF RateLimit header fields.

RateLimit.description: Remaining quota and seconds until the window resets.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying a throttled request.

TooManyRequests.description: The client exceeded the published rate limit.
